rationale: This is a cosmetic variant of the archived NetLiquidKnowledgeValue (identical value leg, liquidity leg changed only from che−(dltt+dlc) to che−dlc−xrd, which also mixes a one-year flow into a stock-based net-cash measure), so it is very unlikely to represent a distinct mechanism from the already-tested t=4.79 result.

The conditioning term is dominated in magnitude and variance by −GROWTH(at,1), so the signal is effectively value × low asset growth — a direct rediscovery of the asset-growth anomaly already spanned by FF5's CMA — and it duplicates the archived BookGrowthHiddenReinvestmentValue's hidden-reinvestment mechanism.

The internal-versus-acquired intangible composition mechanism is already tested in the archive (InternalKnowledgeBookValueQuality, GoodwillCleanBookValue), and this differs only by swapping the value leg from B/M to E/P and gdwl for intan, which is a leg-swap rather than a new economic hypothesis.

A level-relative-to-own-history cost-efficiency conditioner is a substantively different construct from the archived one-period Δ(cogs/revt) version and the sign convention is internally consistent (TS_MIN/current ∈ (0,1], higher = nearer the firm's own efficient frontier), though it is close in spirit to PeakKnowledgeProductivityValue and its incremental information is uncertain.

The conditioning leg is the archived KnowledgeDeleveragingValue's Δleverage term with a small, slowly-varying xrd/at level added, so the cross-sectional ranking will be largely driven by the same deleveraging variable already evaluated (fmb t=4.89, ls_talpha only 1.42) rather than by any genuine R&D-versus-debt substitution.

This is a mechanical recombination of two already-archived legs (PayoutSupportedKnowledgeYield's dividend-plus-R&D yield and KnowledgeDeleveragingValue's knowledge-adjusted leverage change), and the second leg is largely the well-known net-debt-issuance/financing anomaly, so novelty is thin even though the pairing is coherent and untested.
